address: 3450 El Camino Real #105, Santa Clara, CA 95051
w: The Santa Clara El Camino Koreatown go-to for soft-tofu stew: order the soondubu jjigae, a bubbling stone pot of silken tofu in spicy broth cracked with a raw egg, served with a spread of banchan and a stone-pot rice you scrape into nurungji.
sources: yelp.com/biz/sgd-tofu-house-santa-clara - open, updated July 2026 (1,514 reviews); 3450 El Camino Real Ste 105

w: A family-run anchor of historic San Jose Japantown since 1957, doing timeless home-style teishoku; go for the katsudon (crisp pork cutlet over rice bound with egg), the shioyaki salt-grilled fish and light tempura.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-jose - featured in the Best Restaurants in San Jose guide as a Japantown pick for tempura, curry and tonkatsu

w: Downtown Palo Alto's Burmese standby near Stanford; the tossed-tableside tea leaf salad layers fermented laphet with fried garlic, split-pea and yellow-bean crunch, peanuts, sesame and tomato, alongside coconut chicken noohn khao swe.
sources: yelp.com/biz/burma-ruby-palo-alto-3 - open, updated July 2026 (530 reviews); 445 Emerson St
paloaltoonline.com/ae/2014/03/07/review-beautiful-burmese-fare — review of the Burmese restaurant at 445 Emerson (Rangoon/Burma Ruby)

w: One of the South Bay's best izakayas, a boisterous room of shareable Japanese small plates with Italian and Spanish flourishes; the unagi clay-pot rice, hamachi carpaccio and mentaiko dishes are the reasons reservations go fast.
sources: yelp.com/biz/gochi-cupertino-cupertino - open, updated July 2026 (2,400 reviews); 19980 E Homestead Rd

w: A longtime Bay Area tonkotsu destination (originally Santa Clara/Redwood City) now at Los Altos' State Street Market; the signature tonkotsu runs a touch lighter than most so you can finish the pork-bone bowl without reaching for water.
sources: yelp.com/biz/orenchi-ramen-los-altos-hills-2 - open, updated June 2026; relocated to 170 State St, Los Altos (State Street Market)

https://www.kqed.org/bayareabites/89394/bay-area-bites-guide-to-10-favorite-south-bay-ramen-shops (names Orenchi Ramen; KQED article cites the original Santa Clara/Homestead Rd location of the same brand)

address: 3044 El Camino Real, Santa Clara, CA 95051
w: A tabletop grill house in the heart of Santa Clara's El Camino Koreatown, open late; the marinated galbi short rib and pork belly come with a wide banchan spread, and the kitchen also fires shabu-shabu and pajeon.
sources: yelp.com/biz/seorai-korean-bbq-santa-clara - open, updated July 2026 (573 reviews); 3044 El Camino Real

w: The South Bay's most-loved sit-down Filipino spot (a Check, Please! Bay Area pick); the namesake tapsilog pairs sweet-garlicky beef tapa with garlic fried rice and a fried egg, and the sisig and longsilog are just as reliable.
sources: yelp.com/biz/tapsilog-bistro-campbell - open, updated July 2026 (1,619 reviews); 819 W Hamilton Ave, Campbell

address: 26 N San Pedro St, San Jose, CA 95113
w: The downtown San Jose sushi bar off San Pedro Square that locals pack for happy hour; go for fresh nigiri and the over-the-top specialty rolls, with a lively bar scene that has anchored the block since 2016.
sources: yelp.com/biz/sushi-confidential-san-jose-san-jose - open, updated August 2026 (1,195 reviews); 26 N San Pedro St

Sushi Confidential reportedly closing San Pedro Square location — https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/sushi-confidential-san-pedro-square/4119925/ (NOTE: names the 26 N San Pedro St location as closing)

w: A Campbell room that plates both Thai and Cambodian cooking; the curries carry a Khmer accent, and there's a deep vegan menu alongside the pad see ew and tom kha.
sources: yelp.com/biz/thaibodia-bistro-campbell-campbell-2 - open, updated July 2026 (293 reviews); 2200 S Bascom Ave, Campbell

w: The San Jose outpost of the Hokkaido chain inside Mitsuwa Marketplace; the pearl-white tonkotsu simmers around 20 hours, but the shio ramen with a pickled-plum-topped bowl is the one to order.
sources: yelp.com/biz/hokkaido-ramen-santouka-san-jose - open, updated July 2026 (3,438 reviews); 675 Saratoga Ave inside Mitsuwa

w: A homestyle Korean staple in Santa Clara for comforting stews and braises; the galbi jjim (soy-braised short rib) and bone-broth soups come with generous banchan, and it's an easygoing alternative to the El Camino BBQ strip.
sources: yelp.com/biz/kunjip-santa-clara-3 - open, updated August 2026 (2,408 reviews); 1066 Kiely Blvd

address: 642 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA 95128
w: A long-running San Jose Thai institution on Winchester near Santana Row; the pad Thai, panang curry and crispy garlic pork keep the dining room full, and it's a reliable benchmark for the region's Thai canon.
sources: yelp.com/biz/the-original-krung-thai-restaurant-san-jose - open, updated August 2026 (1,309 reviews); 642 S Winchester Blvd

San Jose dining archive / Food & Drink Reader Picks names The Original Krung Thai (est. 1988, S. Winchester) — https://www.metrosiliconvalley.com/archives/restaurants/silicon-valley/siliconvalley-reviews-sanjose.html

w: A tucked-away Midtown Palo Alto room doing Burmese-Chinese home cooking for two decades; the tea leaf salad and coconut-chicken noodles sit next to garlic-forward Chinese plates in an intimate, no-frills space.
sources: yelp.com/biz/green-elephant-gourmet-palo-alto - open, updated June 2026 (335 reviews); 3950 Middlefield Rd

w: An intimate eight-seat omakase counter in downtown Palo Alto led by chef Jiabo Li (formerly Sushi Hon and Sato Omakase); the edomae-style nigiri courses use fish sourced from Japan and beyond, at $105 lunch / $195 dinner.
sources: yelp.com/biz/iki-omakase-palo-alto - open, updated August 2026 (93 reviews); 460 Ramona St, 8-seat counter

w: A family-run turo-turo (point-point) Filipino cafeteria in Sunnyvale since 1993; point at the steam-table trays for crackly lechon, saucy pancit and Shanghai lumpia, then eat it home-style.
sources: yelp.com/biz/rene-rose-island-cuisine-sunnyvale-2 - open, updated June 2026 (307 reviews); 621 Caliente Dr, Sunnyvale

w: A high-volume, all-you-can-eat tabletop grill at Westgate for a crowd; work through spicy bulgogi, marinated short rib and pork belly across a long meat lineup with sides included, open late nightly.
sources: yelp.com/biz/gen-korean-bbq-house-san-jose-3 - open, updated July 2026 (1,499 reviews); 1554 Saratoga Ave (Westgate)

w: Downtown Mountain View's Thai standby (now relocated a few doors down Castro St from its old 174 address); the pad Thai, pineapple curry and coconut prawn soup draw the Castro Street lunch crowd.
sources: yelp.com/biz/amarin-thai-cuisine-mountain-view-3 - open, updated August 2026; current address 147 Castro St (old 174 Castro listing is marked CLOSED)

w: A tiny family-run Japanese room in historic San Jose Japantown; the counter turns out precise sashimi and sushi alongside izakaya-style small plates and comforting donburi, a Japantown insider favorite.
sources: yelp.com/biz/kaita-restaurant-san-jose-2 - open, updated August 2026 (696 reviews); 215 Jackson St, Japantown
